text:
Maya R: Quick one — thinking about standardizing most internal control-plane APIs on gRPC+protobuf for stable contracts and streaming. Biggest worries are gateway patterns, quota enforcement, telemetry, and the rollout UX for client teams. Anyone object?

Tom H: I like gRPC for binary perf and streaming. Browser apps are the obvious caveat — gRPC-web + envoy tends to work but adds ops surface.

Liang C: Proto versioning is doable but we need strict rules: never reuse field numbers, prefer optional/singularity patterns. Also expose JSON fallback for ad-hoc debug.

Ash K: Telemetry note — our tracing headers (x-trace-id / x-span) are HTTP-first. gRPC uses metadata; need to ensure ingress LB and envoy filters propagate them exactly. We saw spans drop in a gRPC path during the last internal rollout.

Noah (sre-bot): FYI: last incident showed missing grpc-status mapping -> alerts didn't trigger. See /incidents/234.

Kevin P: Rollout UX concern: If we silently provide both gRPC and JSON REST, clients might auto-fallback and mask contract/regression issues. We should require client lib opt-in for fallback. Canary should be route-level (not global).

Eva L: Proposed pattern: make proto the canonical source-of-truth. Generate a thin HTTP/JSON shim in the gateway for console/external usage. Gateway responsibilities: schema validation, quota headers, trace propagation, and metrics tagging.

Maya R: Sketch of an envoy route + quota header we discussed in the runbook:
```yaml
route_config:
  name: control-plane
  virtual_hosts:
    - name: api-internal
      domains: ["internal.api.redwood.local"]
      routes:
        - match: { prefix: "/v1/agent" }
          route: { cluster: agent-grpc }
          metadata: { enforce_quota: true }
```
Gateway would translate incoming JSON -> proto, attach `x-quota-key` and forward as grpc metadata.

Tom H: For quotas, we should keep enforcement at the gateway edge (fast rejects) but also emit async accounting from the gRPC services for reconciliation. That prevents quota drift if gateway proxy is bypassed.

Liang C: +1. Also CI step: compile protos in consumer repos and run a compatibility check against the golden proto before release. That will catch accidental breaking changes.

Ash K: For telemetry, here's a tiny patch I used to preserve trace context in envoy:
```json
{"http_filters": [{"name":"envoy.filters.http.grpc_web"}, {"name":"envoy.filters.http.router"} ]}
```
We also need an envoy metadata-to-trace filter to copy metadata->header.

Eva L: Edge case: some downstream infra only accepts JSON and won't speak gRPC at all. We'll maintain autogenerated REST endpoints behind the gateway but mark them as "beta-json" and require an opt-in config on the client side so we can measure usage.

Kevin P: CI/rollout plan idea: 1) proto-only internal clients -> 2) gateway JSON adapter enabled for beta teams -> 3) expose stable REST for console after 90 days of telemetry and schema stability.

Maya R: Agreement check — are we comfortable moving forward with proto-first + gateway shim + quota-at-edge + reconciled accounting + canary route rollouts? react with :+1: or mention concerns.

Tom H: :+1: Need a doc for the client library behavior (explicit fallback opt-in).

Liang C: :+1: Add compatibility CI and proto lint rules.

Ash K: :+1: I'll prototype the envoy filter changes and add integration tests for trace propagation.

Noah (sre-bot): Scheduled alert rule update queued: map grpc-status -> prometheus label for 503/504.

Eva L: I'll draft the gateway validation spec and a sample generated JSON route (for console) and tag it in the PR.

Maya R: sweet. I'll open an RFC with the proposed rollout timeline and requirements (CI checks, envoy changes, quota reconcilers). Thanks everyone.
